title: Yuuna and the Haunted Hot Springs
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Kogarashi, a broke high schooler with spirit-fighting powers, moves into the Yuragi Inn, a former hot-springs inn haunted by the ghost of a girl named Yuuna. Instead of exorcising her, he helps her resolve her unfinished business while meeting the inn's other female tenants, many of them yokai, ninja or exorcists. Yuuna eventually learns who she was and chooses to stay with Kogarashi, whom she marries.
life_message: Compassion and loyalty to those around you, even a ghost, matter more than power or luck.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Fights defend housemates, but most conflicts end in comedy rather than vendetta.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Inn residents live loosely, each with secret powers and private agendas.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Inn tenants form a found family that Kogarashi protects.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Clan and ninja ranks appear but the inn is mostly flat.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Exorcists, yokai lineages and spirit lore drive the plot.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pleasure, romance and personal wishes are celebrated over hardship.

folkways.japan: Onsen inns, yokai folklore and exorcist families are drawn from Japanese folk tradition, and fan-service shonen comedy is a long-running magazine genre in Japan.

delivery.evidence: No review or summary in the sources describes delivery; style inferred from premise and tags (to verify).
delivery.note: Kindness to Yuuna is carried by the plot of a fan-service harem comedy rather than by stated lessons.

winners_losers: Kogarashi and Yuuna win, ending in marriage; evil spirits and Yuuna's regrets lose. Sympathy goes to kindness and loyal companionship.
